title: Fear & Laughter
text:
Now Showing ✦ A Double Feature in Data
Fear & Laughter
Why Americans pay to be scared, and why they pay to laugh
Starring 3,364 Hollywood movies ✦ 1936 to 2018
Presented by Zheyre Tolliver



Admit One ✦ The Thrill
2.7x
The typical horror movie earns back almost three times its budget, the best of any genre.


Admit One ✦ The Relief
1.9x
The typical comedy nearly doubles its money, and studios release one almost every week of the year.











People do not need to be scared or to laugh, yet they buy tickets for both. Psychologists describe horror as a way to feel fear safely: the heart races, the danger is not real, and the relief afterward feels good. Comedy works in the opposite direction, releasing tension and helping people cope with stress.
This site looks at those two genres through what audiences actually did with their money. Out of about 3,300 movies, the typical horror film earned about 2.7 times its budget, the most of any genre, while the typical comedy earned about 1.9 times its budget. Choose your next showing:

title: Find Your Movie
Why October Belongs to Horror
text:
Feature Story











Comedies come out at about the same pace all year, with no month getting more than about 10% of them. Horror is different. Almost one in five horror movies in this data opened in October, more than twice the share of any month in winter. Studios know when audiences are in the mood for fear, and they plan around it.


Almost one in five horror movies opens in October.

That pattern fits what psychologists say about why people enjoy being scared. Halloween makes fear social and playful: haunted houses, costumes, and scary movies are things people do together, in a setting where they know they are safe. In that context a horror film is less a threat and more a shared thrill, and the relief at the end becomes part of the fun.
Comedy does not need a season, because the need it meets, relief from everyday stress, never goes away. Put side by side, the two genres show two different reasons people turn to movies: some feelings we seek out at certain times, and some we need all the time.
